messages:
Simone (sales): Quick sync — ACME Health wants a Private deployment POC. They asked for: privatelink for control plane, VPC peering to our inference VPC, and egress rules for telemetry. Can engineering sketch required subnets/CIDR and DNS flow?
Raj (solutions): For a clean POC we recommend: customer provides at least two subnets (management + gpu), non-overlapping CIDR with our vpc (we'll share ours). Typical minimal sizes: /24 for management, /20 for GPU pool. Also need a route for privatelink interface endpoints to resolve our control plane FQNs.
Taylor (eng-networking): Agree. Notes:
- If using an Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) for control plane, the customer must enable DNS hostnames + private DNS so redwood-control.redwood-inference.com resolves to the endpoint ENIs.
- For VPC peering (inference data path) include route table entries: peer VPC CIDR -> peering connection ID on GPU subnets. No transitive routing.
- If they want outbound internet egress from GPUs (for model downloads/patching), route via NAT GW or egress VPC with TGW.
Raj (solutions): Also clarify which traffic goes over Privatelink vs peering: control/management via PrivateLink (API keys, control plane), inference traffic via peering (low latency). If they insist on encrypting in-flight, we already TLS everything at app layer.
Simone (sales): They asked about IP allowlist for hosted API keys — can we map that to interface endpoint IPs on their side?
Marie (security): Yes but caution: interface endpoint IPs can change if they reassign subnets. Better to allowlist the endpoint security group or use mTLS between customer and control plane. For POC, a static allowlist of current endpoint ENIs is fine but note process in SQA.
Taylor (eng-networking): Practical checklist to give customer:
1) Provide VPC CIDR and available subnets for GPU + management.
2) Create Interface Endpoint (com.amazonaws.region.ec2:interface) for privatelink? (we provide service name).
3) Enable private DNS on endpoint.
4) Add route table entries for peer: Destination = our inference VPC CIDR, Target = pcx-xxxx
5) Security groups: allow TCP 443 from mgmt subnet -> control plane SG, allow gRPC/TCP ports for inference from peer CIDR -> GPU SG.
Include sample route table snippet we can paste:
```
# customer route table for gpu-subnet
Destination       Target
10.0.0.0/16       pcx-0a1b2c3d4e5f
0.0.0.0/0         nat-0b2c3d4e (if using NAT for egress)
```
Simone (sales): They also asked about how API keys are provisioned in Private deploys vs Hosted. Quick note?
Raj (solutions): For Private (VPC) we run a control plane in the customer's network or a private control plane with privatelink. Keys are still issued by Redwood but scoped to the customer's deployment and pinned to project/environment. We can rotate keys on-demand. For Dedicated pools it's similar but keys map to pool tenancy.
Marie (security): Security questionnaire answers to prepare: list of open ports, key rotation policy, where logs are stored (customer can ship to their SIEM), data residency notes, and whether we store any unencrypted tokens (we do not). I'll attach standard SQA snippets.
Simone (sales): Great. Two enterprise blockers I want to preempt: 1) customer insists on AWS PrivateLink without peering (they want all traffic via PrivateLink). Is that feasible for inference throughput?
Taylor (eng-networking): PrivateLink is fine for control plane but not recommended for bulk inference traffic — it incurs ENI scaling, cross-AZ hops and bandwidth limits per AZ. For high-throughput inference we prefer peering or Direct Connect. For POC low TPS it might work but set expectations.
Simone (sales): 2) They want SLA for request latency on POC. Can we give ballpark numbers?
Raj (solutions): For a POC on our Dedicated GPU pool in same region: p50 ~ 50–150ms depending on model/size; p95 will vary. We should ask for their payload sizes and tokens/sec. We'll include test harness to generate realistic load.
Simone (sales): I'll send them the onboarding checklist and request VPC info. Any docs to link?
Raj (solutions): Use internal onboarding doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/pvpc-onboard (shareable) and the public KB: https://redwood.ai/docs/vpc-onboarding. Also add this quick script to validate DNS resolution once PrivateLink is created:
```bash
# from a bastion in customer mgmt subnet
nslookup redwood-control.redwood-inference.com
curl -v https://redwood-control.redwood-inference.com/healthz --resolve 'redwood-control.redwood-inference.com:443:10.2.3.45'
```
Marie (security): I'll prepare the SQA answers and a short note on allowed ciphers + TLS versions.
deploy-bot: deployment note: POC private route template v1 applied for account: acct-12345 by Raj at 2026-03-09T14:22:30Z :gear:
Simone (sales): Perfect — I'll compile this into an email and ask for the VPC CIDRs, desired throughput, and contact for their netops. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
